title: Fresh Fig Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Fresh figs cooked to a jam with lemon zest and blended into a slightly lighter yolk custard instead of vanilla.
summary: A twist on our classic custard: ripe fresh figs are cooked down into a lemony jam and blended into a slightly lighter yolk custard. Sweet, honeyed and a pretty dusky pink.

ingredients.item: ripe fresh figs, stems trimmed, cut into eighths
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon juice, plus more to taste

steps.title: Cook the figs
steps.text: Put the figs, water and lemon zest in the small saucepan, cover and cook over medium heat for 8-10 min, stirring occasionally, until soft.

steps.title: Make the jam
steps.text: Uncover, add the 60 g sugar and keep cooking, stirring often, for about 10 min until thick and jammy. Leave to cool.

steps.title: Start the custard
steps.text: Heat the cream and milk until steaming. Whisk the yolks with the 90 g sugar and the salt, whisk in a third of the hot dairy, then return it all to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir gently over low heat, scraping the base, until it thickens to 77-80 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain into a bowl, cool in the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the cold custard with the fig jam and lemon juice until smooth. Taste and add a little more lemon juice if it tastes flat.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Use very ripe, soft figs; underripe ones give little flavour.
A common mistake is stopping the jam too early. It should look thick and glossy, or the ice cream will be icy.
Dark-skinned figs give the deepest colour.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
